rawFindings.title: HTML error formatting mutates the live route descriptor
rawFindings.explanation: When `params.request.themeRoute` already exists, this assignment keeps the same object and the formatter later sets `params.request.themeRoute.handler = 'render'`. In the middleware path, `req.themeRoute` is the registered route descriptor object, so rendering an HTML error now permanently overwrites that route's configured handler for subsequent requests.
rawFindings.suggestion: Clone the existing themeRoute before modifying it, e.g. `params.request.themeRoute = params.request.themeRoute ? util.clone(params.request.themeRoute) : {};`.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: A route registered with `handler: 'show'` handles `/example`. If an HTML error is rendered during one request to `/example`, the formatter changes the stored descriptor's handler to `render`; the next normal GET `/example` invokes `render` instead of `show` or fails if the controller has no `render` method.
